sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A personal reading list fits in a link's fragment
sections.para: I want to send people a link saying from Dinis, for Steve, here is what to read, adding the personal 10 to 20% the newsroom's curation lacks. The article holds a brief for the newsroom, a brief for the RiskMandate agent, and an account of the loop that ships such features in a day.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Names and article numbers ride in the fragment, untracked
sections.para: The link carries names and stable article numbers after the #, which browsers never send to the server, and opens as a removable persona. Anyone can make a list; the RiskMandate agent drafts and I send. Nothing tracks the reader, and this week the loop shipped personas by link 17 hours after their brief.

sections.label: Part one: the brief for the newsroom
sections.line: Stable numbers, a fragment-read page and a list maker
sections.para: Every article gets a permanent number in a growing ids.json, enforced by a build gate, and a /for/ page reads from, to, r, s and f from the fragment, validates them, and opens the list as a removable visitor persona. A make page builds links in the browser. No accounts, endpoints or tracking.

sections.label: Part two: the brief for the RiskMandate agent
sections.line: The agent researches, picks articles and drafts; Dinis sends
sections.para: Once /for/ is live, the RiskMandate agent proposes contacts, researches public sources, picks three to seven articles with a reason for each, builds and tests the link, and drafts a short email that passes the second reader. Dinis approves and sends. One person, one list, one email, with nothing private in the link.

sections.label: Part three: the loop
sections.line: Written briefs and small contracts close the loop daily
sections.para: Editorial, product, engineering, sales and the founder usually take weeks. Here hand-offs are written briefs, each part owns its repository or vault, and contracts like article numbers let parts move independently. This week a brief shipped in 17 hours and corrections followed payments within 32 minutes; parts drift, sessions run out, and I remain the router.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: a voice memo, git logs and related articles
sections.para: Drafted from a voice memo of 11 October 2026 by this site's agent, with the argument and decisions mine. The reading list figure is an illustrative mock, loop timings come from git logs, and the fragment behaviour is RFC 3986 section 3.5.
